text:
maria: Quick heads-up — saw sustained egress from a private-deploy customer during last week's load test. Traffic to a couple of external telemetry hosts looks unexpected. Need a short mitigation + triage plan: netpol tightening, audit sampling bump, RBAC for keystore access, and vuln triage on a keystore dependency. Who can take what this afternoon? cc @samir @aj

aj: Which customer? can you paste the flow logs and dest IPs?
maria: Customer (anonymized): cust-phi-3. Dest IPs: 54.210.123.45, 52.23.87.190. Flow log snippet:```
2026-03-18T14:02:12Z src=10.0.45.12:46722 dst=54.210.123.45:443 proto=TCP action=ACCEPT bytes=1200
2026-03-18T14:02:13Z src=10.0.45.12:46723 dst=52.23.87.190:443 proto=TCP action=ACCEPT bytes=2100
```
ops_ella: Ugh. Let's treat this as egress policy gap. Immediate mitigation: deny-by-default egress NetworkPolicy for the customer's namespace, allow only curated endpoints (redwood telemetry + known mirrors). I can draft a policy.
samir: For keystore / KMS access: propose a short-lived proxy role `keystore:decrypt-only` that only allows Decrypt, no encrypt/sign. Throttle token TTL to 5m and instrument proxy to log token_id + src_pod. That reduces blast radius if creds leak.
harvey: Ran a vuln scan yesterday — the keystore client dependency flagged CVE-2026-0421 (library `keystore-dep` 2.1.3). Fix available in 2.1.5. Recommend canary patch asap.
maria: OK plan outline: 1) push deny-by-default netpol to affected namespaces (ops_ella) 2) bump keystore-decrypt audit sampling to 100% for cust-phi-3 and route to SIEM (ops_ella + sec) 3) create `keystore:decrypt-only` proxy + short TTL (samir) 4) patch keystore-dep in canary -> full rollout (harvey) 5) run tabletop and update incident runbook to include key-rotation threshold (maria)
samir: I'll own the RBAC proxy + test harness. ETA: EOD for a minimal proxy image and helm chart.
aj: I'll upload the draft netpol PR in ~30m, ping for quick reviews. PR: http://git.internal/redwood/netpol/pulls/1234 (will add selectors)
ops_ella: SIEM fields we need for the decrypt alert: `[user_id, svc_account, src_pod, dest_kms, tok_id, decrypt_count_1m, geo]`. I'll set retention to 90 days for decrypts tied to private deploys.
sec-bot: Runbook created: https://confluence.internal/redwood/priv-egress-observability-runbook — includes steps for netpol rollback, k8s audit sample increase, and keystore rotation checklist. Automated ticket #SEC-872 created.
maria: One addition — if decrypt anomalies > 10/min for a given svc_account, runbook step 4 says to rotate keystore wrapping key and revoke service tokens. Please add that as explicit action.
harvey: Will run tabletop tomorrow 10:30am. I'll invite ops, platform, and a dev from the affected customer team.
aj: Netpol draft pushed. Key snippet:```yaml
kind: NetworkPolicy
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-by-default
  namespace: cust-phi-3
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: [] # deny all egress by default
```
ops_ella: We'll then add allow rules for: redwood-agent telemetry, image registries, internal logging endpoints. Keep rules explicit and minimal.
samir: QA note: the RBAC proxy must preserve tok_id in logs and propagate a hashed user_id to SIEM to avoid leaking raw PII.
maria: Thanks everyone. After patch and netpol, we'll schedule a short postmortem: root cause = weak default egress posture + an outdated keystore dep in a customer-side image. Action owners above.
ops_ella: +1. I'll coordinate SIEM alerts and make sure detection rule triggers before we finish rollout.
harvey: Ack. I'll handle the canary patch rollout and monitor metrics: decrypt latency, decrypt error rate, and unexpected egress counts.
maria: If anyone finds further anomalies (extra hosts, different ports), drop here and tag @maria. :thumbsup:
aj: ack
samir: ack
ops_ella: ack
harvey: ack
